ENGLISH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #11
====

GRADE: Grade 7
SUBJECT: ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.

2. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.

3. When practising Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives.

4. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goes
   B. going
   C. went
   D. goed

5. When practising Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness.

6. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. No full stops
   B. One main idea with supporting sentences
   C. Only one word repeated
   D. Many unrelated topics with no link

7. When practising Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.

8. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.

9. When practising Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

10. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.

11. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. quickly
   B. happiness
   C. blue
   D. run

12. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 12.5.1 The Writing Process: Dialogues and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 13.1.1 Listening Comprehension: Extensive Listening and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 13.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension Strategies and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Sentences: Simple Sentences and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
